sections.heading: India's energy needs, deficit, resources & dependence

blocks.text: India is the **world's third-largest energy consumer**, with rapidly rising demand. It relies heavily on **coal and imported oil/gas**, faces an **energy deficit and import dependence**, and is pivoting towards **renewables** for security and sustainability.

rows: **Coal dominant (~55% of power)**; oil & gas largely imported; growing renewables.
India imports **~85% of crude oil** and much natural gas.
Coal (large reserves), limited oil/gas, hydro, solar/wind potential, uranium/thorium.
**Conventional** (coal, oil, gas, nuclear, hydro) vs **non-conventional/renewable** (solar, wind, bio).
**Energy security + net-zero by 2070**; 500 GW non-fossil by 2030.

prelimsPointers: India is the **world's 3rd-largest energy consumer**.
**Coal** dominates power generation (~55%); India imports **~85% of its crude oil**.
Energy sources — **conventional (coal, oil, gas, nuclear, hydro)** vs **non-conventional (solar, wind, bio, geothermal)**.
India has vast **coal & thorium** reserves but limited oil/gas.
Target — **500 GW non-fossil capacity by 2030**; **net-zero by 2070**.
**Energy security** = reliable, affordable, sustainable supply.
Nodal ministry — **Ministry of Power / New & Renewable Energy (MNRE)**.

glossary.definition: Reliable, affordable and sustainable access to energy.
Traditional sources like coal, oil, gas, nuclear and hydro.
Reliance on foreign supply, e.g. India importing ~85% of its crude oil.

blocks.text: India's **energy policy** aims at **access, security, efficiency and sustainability** through a suite of programmes — renewable-energy missions, efficiency schemes, and electrification drives — steering the country towards a clean-energy transition.

rows: Part of NAPCC; large solar-capacity targets.
Solar pumps & grid-connected solar for farmers.
**International Solar Alliance, Green Hydrogen Mission, ethanol blending, PAT scheme, UDAY**.

prelimsPointers: **National Solar Mission** — under the National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC).
**Saubhagya** — household electrification; **DDUGJY** — rural electrification.
**PM-KUSUM** — solar pumps for farmers; **UJALA** — LED distribution (BEE).
**International Solar Alliance (ISA)** — India-France; HQ **Gurugram**.
**National Green Hydrogen Mission**; **ethanol blending (E20 by 2025-26)**.
**PAT (Perform, Achieve, Trade)** scheme — industrial energy efficiency.
**UDAY** — discom financial revival; **BEE** — Bureau of Energy Efficiency (star labels).

glossary.definition: The India-France-led alliance (HQ Gurugram) promoting solar energy globally.
A scheme providing solar pumps and solar power to farmers.
India's programme to become a hub for clean hydrogen production.

blocks.text: **Solar, wind and nuclear** are the pillars of India's low-carbon energy strategy. Solar and wind are **renewable**; nuclear is a **clean but non-renewable** high-density source, with India pursuing a distinctive **thorium-based three-stage** programme.

rows: Photovoltaic/thermal; India among world leaders; **Bhadla (Rajasthan)** among world's largest solar parks.
India a top-5 wind-power nation; **Tamil Nadu, Gujarat** lead.
**Homi Bhabha's 3-stage programme** — PHWR (uranium) → FBR (plutonium) → **thorium**; India has vast thorium.
**Tarapur, Kudankulam (largest), Kaiga, Kakrapar**; regulated by **AERB**; run by **NPCIL**.

prelimsPointers: **Solar** — India a global leader; **Bhadla Solar Park (Rajasthan)** among the world's largest.
**Wind** — India a top-5 nation; leaders **Tamil Nadu & Gujarat**.
**Homi Bhabha's 3-stage nuclear programme** — **Stage 1 PHWR (uranium), Stage 2 FBR (plutonium), Stage 3 thorium**.
India has among the **world's largest thorium reserves** (Kerala monazite sands).
**Kudankulam (Tamil Nadu)** — India's largest nuclear plant; others — Tarapur, Kaiga, Kakrapar.
**NPCIL** operates plants; **AERB** regulates nuclear safety.
Solar & wind are **renewable**; nuclear is **clean but non-renewable**.

glossary.definition: Homi Bhabha's plan progressing from uranium PHWRs to plutonium FBRs to thorium reactors.
Technology converting sunlight directly into electricity.
The Atomic Energy Regulatory Board overseeing nuclear safety in India.

sections.heading: Environmental issues, legal aspects, policies & treaties

blocks.text: India addresses **environmental issues** through a framework of **constitutional provisions, laws (EPA, Air/Water Acts), institutions (NGT, CPCB) and international treaties** — balancing development with ecological protection.

rows: **Environment (Protection) Act 1986, Water Act 1974, Air Act 1981, Wildlife Protection Act 1972, Forest Conservation Act 1980**.
**Stockholm (1972), Rio (1992), Montreal (ozone), Basel, Ramsar (wetlands), CITES, UNFCCC/Paris, CBD**.

prelimsPointers: **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986** — umbrella law (after the Bhopal disaster).
**Water Act 1974, Air Act 1981, Wildlife Protection Act 1972, Forest Conservation Act 1980**.
**National Green Tribunal (NGT), 2010** — environmental adjudication.
**CPCB/SPCB** — pollution control boards; **MoEFCC** — nodal ministry.
Treaties — **Montreal (ozone), Basel (hazardous waste), Ramsar (wetlands), CITES (species trade), Stockholm (POPs)**.
**Art. 48A & 51A(g)** — environment in DPSP & Fundamental Duties.
**EIA** (Environmental Impact Assessment) mandatory for major projects.

glossary.definition: The Environment (Protection) Act, India's umbrella environmental law.
The National Green Tribunal (2010) for speedy environmental justice.
The international treaty for the conservation of wetlands.

blocks.text: **Biodiversity** is the variety of life — genes, species and ecosystems. India is a **megadiverse country** with rich biological wealth, but faces serious threats from **habitat loss, poaching, invasive species and climate change**, prompting conservation laws and initiatives.

rows: One of **17 megadiverse countries**; **4 biodiversity hotspots** (Himalaya, Western Ghats, Indo-Burma, Sundaland/Nicobar).
Ecosystem services, food, medicine, climate regulation, livelihoods.
**Habitat loss, poaching, pollution, invasive species, climate change**.
**In-situ (parks, reserves), ex-situ (zoos, gene banks); Biological Diversity Act 2002; NBA**.

prelimsPointers: Three levels — **genetic, species, ecosystem** diversity.
India is one of **17 megadiverse nations**; has **4 biodiversity hotspots** — **Himalaya, Western Ghats, Indo-Burma, Sundaland (Nicobar)**.
**In-situ** conservation (national parks, sanctuaries, biosphere reserves) vs **ex-situ** (zoos, seed/gene banks).
**Biological Diversity Act, 2002**; **National Biodiversity Authority (NBA, Chennai)**.
Threats — **habitat loss, poaching, invasive species, pollution, climate change**.
**IUCN Red List** categorises threatened species (CR, EN, VU).
**Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD, 1992)** — Rio; Nagoya Protocol (access & benefit sharing).

glossary.definition: The variety of life at genetic, species and ecosystem levels.
A biologically rich but threatened region; India has four.
Protecting species in their natural habitat (parks, reserves).
